summary: Pit crew animation state processor. Runs once (guarded by bit 0 of this+0x0): iterates the child animation-entry array (count at this+0xC, array pointer at this+0x10, stride 120 bytes), resets each live entry's keyframe animation to time 0.0 via sub_4A2840, clears or sets a visibility/flag bit on the entry's associated widget based on the entry's active-state byte, and frees animation state resources when the entry is flagged inactive. After the loop, if global detail level dword_7CF884 >= 2 and the widget-update guard this+0x14 is non-zero, recursively updates the UI widget tree. Finally marks the executed bit.

operations.description: Guard on bit 0 of this+0x0: if already set (previously executed) the entire function body is skipped and only this+0xC is returned.
Loop guard: read entry count from this+0xC and iterate only while it is greater than zero.
do-while loop over the count of entries, walking the child animation-entry array at this+0x10 with a fixed stride of 120 bytes per entry.
Compute the current child entry pointer as this+0x10 base plus the loop index; read the entry's widget/flag pointer at entry+100 to test liveness.
Call sub_4A2840 on the current child entry with 0.0 to reset its keyframe animation to the start.
Guard on the caller flag a2 OR the child entry's active-state byte at entry+3: only entries considered active proceed to the flag update.
On the entry's associated widget pointer (entry+100), clear the visibility bit via BitClear when the entry's byte at +2 is set, otherwise set the bit via Bit12FlagSet.
When the child entry's field at +72 is not -1 and its widget pointer at +100 is non-zero, call sub_5506A0(0, 0, 0) to clear/reset the entry's animation state resources.
Guard: only when global detail level dword_7CF884 is >= 2 and the widget-update guard field this+0x14 is non-zero does the recursive UI widget update run.
Call UIWidgetRecursiveStateUpdate(1, 0, 0) to recursively refresh UI widget tree visibility state.
Set bit 0 of this+0x0 so the function executes only once.
Return the entry count this+0xC (or the result of the UI update call when it ran).
